prompt: The ancient Maya civilization was centered in which region?
choices: The Andes Mountains of South America
The Great Plains of North America
explain: The Maya lived in southern Mexico (including the Yucatan Peninsula) and in Guatemala, Belize, Honduras, and El Salvador.

prompt: What kind of writing did the ancient Maya use?
choices: The Latin alphabet used in English
They had no way to record words
explain: The Maya wrote with hieroglyphic signs. Scholars can now read much of what they wrote.

prompt: Maya books written on paper made from tree bark are called what?
explain: The Maya made paper from the inner bark of wild fig trees and wrote books on it. These books are called codices.

prompt: Why do only four Maya books (codices) survive today?
choices: They were all buried in pyramids on purpose
Spanish priests destroyed most of them
explain: Maya books existed before the Spanish conquest, but Spanish priests destroyed most of them. Only four are known to survive.

prompt: How many days were in the sacred Maya calendar?
explain: The Maya sacred calendar had 260 days, made of 13 cycles of 20 named days.

prompt: Which three crops were the base of Maya farming?
explain: By about 1500 BCE the Maya were farming corn (maize), beans, and squash.

prompt: The ancient Maya city of Tikal is in which country today?
explain: Tikal is in the rainforest of northern Guatemala. It was the largest city in the southern Maya lowlands.

prompt: The ancient city of Chichen Itza is on which peninsula?
explain: Chichen Itza is on the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico. It is now a World Heritage site.

prompt: The Olmec are famous for carving what?
explain: The Olmec carved colossal stone heads, some as tall as 9 feet.

prompt: Where did the Olmec civilization develop?
choices: The hot lowlands along the Gulf of Mexico
explain: The Olmec lived in the hot, humid lowlands along the Gulf of Mexico, in what is now southern Mexico.

prompt: What was the name of the Aztec capital city?
explain: The Aztec built their great capital, Tenochtitlan, in central Mexico.

prompt: The Aztec built their capital, Tenochtitlan, on an island in what?
explain: Tenochtitlan was founded around 1325 on an island in Lake Texcoco.

prompt: Which modern city stands where the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan once was?
explain: Tenochtitlan was in the area of modern-day Mexico City.

prompt: What were Aztec chinampas?
choices: Small farm islands built in a lake
explain: Chinampas were artificial islands made from layers of plants, dirt, and mud. Farmers grew crops on them.

prompt: What language did the Aztec speak?
explain: The Aztec spoke Nahuatl.

prompt: Who was the Aztec emperor when Hernan Cortes arrived?
explain: Montezuma II was the Aztec emperor. Cortes took him hostage in Tenochtitlan in 1519.

prompt: In what year did Hernan Cortes and his forces conquer the Aztec capital?
explain: Cortes arrived in 1519. By 1521 his forces and their Indigenous allies had taken Tenochtitlan.

prompt: Which disease, brought by Europeans, killed many Aztec people and helped the Spanish win?
explain: The Aztec had no immunity to smallpox. The disease killed huge numbers of them.

prompt: In 1978, a large carved stone disk was found in Mexico City. Digging there uncovered which Aztec site?
choices: The Templo Mayor, the great pyramid of Tenochtitlan
explain: The 1978 discovery of a stone disk showing the goddess Coyolxauhqui started the full dig of the Templo Mayor.

prompt: What was the capital of the Inca Empire?
explain: Cusco, in Peru, was the Inca capital. It is one of the oldest cities in the Western Hemisphere.

prompt: What language did the Inca speak?
explain: The Inca spoke Quechua. Their descendants in the Andes still speak it today.

prompt: The Inca Empire was built in which mountain range?
explain: The Inca Empire ran along the Andes Mountains and the Pacific coast of South America.

prompt: What was an Inca quipu?
choices: A set of knotted cords used to keep records
explain: Quipus were cords with knots. The knots stood for numbers.

prompt: Inca officials used quipus to record what kind of information?
choices: Maps of the stars for sailors
Taxes, census counts, and storehouse supplies
explain: Quipus recorded facts like taxes, how many people lived in a place, and what was in storehouses.

prompt: Machu Picchu is in which country?
explain: Machu Picchu is in the Andes Mountains of Peru, about 50 miles from Cusco.

prompt: Which Spanish conquistador conquered the Inca Empire?
explain: Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor in 1532. This let Spain take over the Inca Empire.

prompt: Which Inca emperor was captured by Francisco Pizarro in 1532?
explain: Pizarro captured Atahualpa at Cajamarca in 1532. He was the last free-ruling Inca emperor.

prompt: Mesa Verde National Park, with its cliff dwellings, is in which state?
explain: Mesa Verde is in southwestern Colorado. It protects cliff dwellings built by the Ancestral Pueblo people.

prompt: Which people built the cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde?
explain: The Ancestral Pueblo people built homes in the cliffs at Mesa Verde over 700 years ago.

prompt: In what year did Mesa Verde become a national park?
explain: President Theodore Roosevelt made Mesa Verde a national park on June 29, 1906.

prompt: What is the largest cliff dwelling at Mesa Verde?
explain: Cliff Palace is the largest cliff dwelling in the park. It is nearly 800 years old.

prompt: By about the year 1300, what had most of the people of Mesa Verde done?
choices: Built a new city on Lake Texcoco
Moved south to what is now New Mexico and Arizona
explain: By 1300, most of the people had left Mesa Verde and moved south into what is now New Mexico and Arizona.

prompt: The Ancestral Pueblo people lived where Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, and Utah meet. What is this area called?
explain: The place where four states meet is called the Four Corners. The Ancestral Pueblo culture centered there.

prompt: In what year did Christopher Columbus make his first voyage across the Atlantic?
explain: Columbus made his first voyage in 1492-93. He made four voyages in all.

prompt: Which country's king and queen paid for Columbus's voyages?
explain: King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella of Spain supported Columbus.

prompt: What was Columbus trying to reach by sailing west across the Atlantic?
explain: Columbus wanted Spain to reach Asia by sailing west instead of going around Africa.

prompt: Which ship was Columbus's flagship on his first voyage?
explain: The Santa Maria was Columbus's flagship. The Nina and Pinta sailed with it.

prompt: Columbus reached the island he named Hispaniola in 1492. Which two countries share that island today?
explain: Haiti is on the western third of Hispaniola. The Dominican Republic is on the eastern two-thirds.

prompt: The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) divided newly found lands between which two countries?
explain: The treaty drew a line on the map. Spain got lands to the west of it and Portugal got lands to the east.

prompt: In 1500, Pedro Alvares Cabral claimed which land for Portugal?
explain: Cabral, a Portuguese navigator, reached Brazil on April 22, 1500, and claimed it for Portugal. That is one reason Brazil speaks Portuguese.

prompt: Ferdinand Magellan led the first expedition to do what?
choices: Sail all the way around the world
explain: Magellan led the first expedition to sail around the globe. He was killed on the way, and Juan Sebastian Elcano finished the trip in 1522.

prompt: The Columbian Exchange began in 1492. What was it?
choices: A trade deal that made Columbus rich
The movement of plants, animals, and diseases between the Americas and the rest of the world
A swap of land between Canada and Mexico
explain: After Columbus's voyages, crops, animals, and germs moved across the Atlantic in both directions.

prompt: Which foods went from the Americas to the rest of the world in the Columbian Exchange?
explain: Corn, potatoes, tomatoes, peanuts, and chili peppers came from the Americas.

prompt: Which animals did the Columbian Exchange bring to the Americas?
explain: Europeans brought horses, pigs, cattle, goats, and sheep. Horses changed life for Plains Indians.

prompt: Why did so many Indigenous people in the Americas die after Europeans arrived?
choices: They had no immunity to diseases like smallpox and measles
They were hit by a giant earthquake
explain: Native people had never faced diseases like smallpox, measles, and influenza. Many communities lost half or more of their people.

prompt: Samuel de Champlain founded which city in 1608?
explain: Champlain founded Quebec in 1608. He is called the Father of New France.

prompt: Jacques Cartier explored the St. Lawrence River for which country?
explain: Cartier sailed for King Francis I of France. His trips helped France claim land in North America.

prompt: Before it became Haiti, the colony of Saint-Domingue belonged to which country?
explain: Saint-Domingue was a French colony. After its people won independence, it became the country of Haiti.

prompt: Toussaint Louverture, a leader of the Haitian Revolution, was born into what?
explain: Toussaint Louverture was born enslaved in Saint-Domingue. He became the main leader of the revolt.

prompt: In what year did Haiti declare its independence?
explain: Jean-Jacques Dessalines declared Haiti independent in 1804.

prompt: Haiti was the first country founded by whom?
explain: Haiti won independence from France and became the first country founded by people who had been enslaved.

prompt: Simon Bolivar was given what nickname?
explain: Bolivar was named El Libertador, The Liberator, after he took Caracas from Spanish forces in 1813.

prompt: Which South American country is named after Simon Bolivar?
explain: Bolivia is named for Simon Bolivar.

prompt: Miguel Hidalgo, called the father of Mexican independence, had what job?
explain: Miguel Hidalgo was a Roman Catholic priest who led the start of Mexico's fight for independence.

prompt: Miguel Hidalgo's famous speech, the Grito de Dolores, was given on which date now celebrated as Mexican Independence Day?
explain: On September 16, 1810, Hidalgo called for an end to Spanish rule. Mexico celebrates that date as Independence Day.

prompt: Brazil declared independence in 1822 from which country?
explain: Brazil had been ruled by Portugal. Dom Pedro declared Brazil independent on September 7, 1822.

prompt: On July 1, 1867, which new country was formed by joining Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick?
explain: Canada was formed on July 1, 1867. Canadians now celebrate that day as Canada Day.

prompt: The Panama Canal connects which two oceans?
explain: The canal cuts across Panama so ships can go between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

prompt: In what year was the Panama Canal completed?
explain: Work under U.S. supervision began in 1904, and the canal was completed in 1914.

prompt: The Amazon River empties into which ocean?
explain: The Amazon starts in the Andes of Peru and flows east across South America into the Atlantic.

prompt: What is a primary source?
choices: A first-hand record made by someone who took part in or saw an event
A book written much later about an event
A website that explains old events
explain: Primary sources come from people who were there. Diaries, photos, and speeches are examples.

prompt: Which of these is a secondary source?
choices: A book written today about Abraham Lincoln
A letter written by a soldier in 1863
explain: A secondary source is made after an event by someone who was not there. A modern book about Lincoln is secondary.

prompt: What is an artifact?
choices: A story passed down by talking
A map drawn from a satellite
An object that people in the past made, used, or left behind
explain: Artifacts are things people made and left behind, like pottery, tools, and beads. They help us learn how people lived.

prompt: What is oral tradition?
choices: Passing down knowledge and stories by speaking and listening
explain: Oral tradition passes knowledge, stories, and ideas from person to person through speech.

prompt: What can archaeologists learn by studying artifacts?
choices: Where people lived, what they ate, and what they wore
Exactly what people were thinking each day
The names of every person who lived there
What the weather will be next year
explain: Artifacts can tell us where people lived, what they ate, wore, and used, and how cultures changed.

prompt: What did the Olmec build to carry water into their cities and fields?
explain: The Olmec built aqueducts to bring water into their cities and to water their fields.

prompt: The Maya civilization declined by about 900 CE. Which causes does a history textbook give?
choices: Poor soil and a long drought
explain: Poor soil and a drought that lasted almost two centuries weakened the Maya. The Spanish and smallpox did not arrive until the 1500s.

prompt: The Maya improved a calendar and a written language that which earlier people had started?
explain: The Olmec began a calendar and writing, and the Maya perfected them.

prompt: In what year did the Aztec begin building their capital, Tenochtitlan?
explain: The Aztec began building Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco in 1325.

prompt: Besides gold, what did the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan take in from surrounding peoples?
explain: Tenochtitlan was very wealthy and took in tribute, or required payments, from nearby peoples.

prompt: How did the Inca ruler get public works like roads built?
choices: Enslaved Africans were brought across the Atlantic
Each peasant worked for the ruler some days every month
Traders from Europe built them for pay
explain: Inca peasants owed the ruler a number of days of work each month on public works projects.

prompt: How did the Inca make farmland on steep mountain slopes?
choices: They built floating farm islands in lakes
They burned rain forest to clear it
They cut terraces into the mountains
explain: The Inca farmed terraced land that they cut into the steep Andes. Floating farm islands were an Aztec method.

prompt: By about 1050 CE, Chaco Canyon had become the center of which people's civilization?
explain: Chaco Canyon became the main center of Ancestral Pueblo civilization by about 1050 CE.

prompt: Chaco Culture National Historical Park, with its ancient great houses, is in which state?
explain: Chaco Canyon is in northwestern New Mexico.

prompt: What is Pueblo Bonito at Chaco Canyon?
choices: A multistory stone great house with hundreds of rooms
explain: Pueblo Bonito is one of the great houses at Chaco: a stone building several stories tall with hundreds of rooms.

prompt: In which river valley did the Hopewell culture reach its peak?
explain: The Hopewell lived in what is now the Ohio River Valley.

prompt: The Hopewell culture flourished from about 1 to 400 CE. What did these people build?
choices: Earthen walls and mounds, often in geometric shapes
Stone pyramids with temples on top
explain: Hopewell groups built earthworks made of earthen walls and ditches, often in geometric patterns, along with mounds.

prompt: Hopewell people got which of these goods through trade with faraway places?
choices: Obsidian, copper, mica, and sea shells
explain: Hopewell trade brought in mica, obsidian, copper, shark teeth, and sea shells. Horses, steel, and Spanish silver came over a thousand years later.

prompt: The ancient city of Cahokia is in which state today?
explain: Cahokia Mounds is in southwestern Illinois, across the Mississippi River from St. Louis.

prompt: Cahokia was the main city of which culture?
explain: Cahokia was the main center of the Middle Mississippian culture, which flourished from about 950 to 1350 CE.

prompt: What is Monks Mound?
choices: A huge earthen mound at Cahokia
A cliff dwelling at Mesa Verde
explain: Monks Mound at Cahokia is the largest human-made earthen structure in North America, about 100 feet high.

prompt: The ancient city of Cahokia was built on the floodplain of which river?
explain: Cahokia Mounds sits on the Mississippi River floodplain.

prompt: Effigy Mounds National Monument in Iowa has mounds built in what shapes?
explain: Effigy mounds are earthen mounds shaped like animals. A bear mound can be seen along the park trail.

prompt: Among the Iroquois, what role did women have in choosing a chief?
choices: Women had no part in it
The Aztec emperor chose the chief
Women selected and advised the chief
explain: In tribes such as the Iroquois, women had power and usually selected and counseled the chief.

prompt: How did horses change life for Plains peoples?
choices: They made it easier to follow and hunt huge bison herds
They pulled plows on large wheat farms
They carried silver from mountain mines
They let people stop moving and build stone cities
explain: Horses let Plains peoples follow and hunt the huge bison herds more easily.

prompt: Which Europeans first brought the horses that Plains peoples later rode?
explain: Horses were first brought to the Americas by the Spanish.

prompt: Many Inuit spent the winter in houses made of snow blocks. What are these called?
explain: Snow-block houses are called igloos. In summer many Inuit lived in animal-skin tents.

prompt: To stay warm in the Arctic, the Inuit made clothing from what?
explain: The Inuit made warm, fitted clothing from caribou fur and sealskin.

prompt: Inuit hunters often hunted seals from what kind of small boat?
explain: Inuit hunters used harpoons to hunt seals on the ice or from kayaks.

prompt: The ancient city of Teotihuacan is known for which two huge pyramids?
choices: The Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon
The Templo Mayor and Machu Picchu
explain: Teotihuacan's plazas and temples are dominated by the Pyramid of the Moon and the huge Pyramid of the Sun.

prompt: The ruins of Teotihuacan are about 30 miles northeast of which modern city?
explain: Teotihuacan is about 30 miles (50 km) northeast of Mexico City.

prompt: Prince Henry the Navigator led exploration of Africa and the Atlantic in the 1400s for which country?
explain: Prince Henry the Navigator led Portugal's exploration in the 1400s.

prompt: After crossing the Atlantic, on October 12, 1492, Columbus landed on an island in which island group?
explain: On October 12, 1492, Columbus made landfall on an island in the Bahamas.

prompt: Which Native people joined Hernan Cortes and helped him fight the Aztec?
explain: The Tlaxcalan sided with the Spanish and sent many fighters to the siege of Tenochtitlan.

prompt: Who was Malintzin, also called La Malinche?
choices: A Taino chief who met Columbus
A Nahua woman who helped Cortes
A Spanish queen who paid for voyages
explain: Malintzin was a Nahua woman who aided Cortes. Her Spanish name was Dona Marina.

prompt: Francisco Vazquez de Coronado led a large expedition into what area?
choices: The St. Lawrence River in Canada
The lands north of Mexico City
explain: Coronado led Spaniards and Native allies into the lands north of Mexico City.

prompt: From 1539 to 1542, Hernando de Soto explored the southeastern United States looking for what?
explain: De Soto led expeditions through the Southeast looking for gold.

prompt: Which crop did Columbus bring to Hispaniola in 1493?
explain: Columbus brought sugar to Hispaniola in 1493. Potatoes, corn, and tobacco were already American plants.

prompt: The Aztec used the seeds of which plant as money?
explain: Chocolate is made from cacao seeds, which the Aztec used as money.

prompt: What was a Spanish encomienda?
choices: A legal right to make Native people work, given to conquistadors
explain: Spain gave encomiendas, legal rights to Native labor, to conquistadors who served the crown.

prompt: Spaniards found rich veins of which metal in the mountain called Potosi?
explain: The Spanish found rich silver ore at Potosi in South America.

prompt: Which European country was the first to carry large numbers of captive Africans across the Atlantic?
explain: The Portuguese were the first to ship large numbers of enslaved Africans across the Atlantic.

prompt: What name did Jacques Cartier give to the northern North American lands he claimed?
explain: Cartier claimed northern North America for France and named it New France.

prompt: Samuel de Champlain made an alliance with which Native peoples?
explain: Champlain allied with the Huron confederacy and the Algonquins and fought beside them.

prompt: The French fur trade in North America depended most on the pelts of which animal?
explain: Native hunters traded furs, especially beaver pelts, for French goods.

prompt: The Dutch colony of New Netherland had its headquarters at New Amsterdam on which island?
explain: New Amsterdam was on the island of Manhattan.

prompt: When Henry Hudson explored the river now named for him, what was he looking for?
explain: Hudson was searching for a northwest passage to Asia. The furs he found led the Dutch to claim the area.

prompt: What were English privateers?
choices: Sea captains allowed by their government to raid enemy ships
explain: Privateers had their government's permission to raid enemy ships. English privateers plundered Spanish ships in the Caribbean.

prompt: In 1542, Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo sailed into what is now San Diego Bay and claimed the land for which country?
explain: Cabrillo led the first European expedition along the coast of the western United States and claimed the land for Spain.

prompt: Spanish missions along the San Antonio River changed local life by bringing what?
choices: A new religion, farming, and settled communities
explain: The missions brought a new religion, farming, and settled communities to the Native people there.

prompt: The San Antonio missions were on the northern edge of which Spanish territory?
explain: The five San Antonio missions, begun in 1718, were on the northern edge of New Spain.

prompt: In 1513, Vasco Nunez de Balboa became the first European to see which ocean?
explain: In 1513 Balboa became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean and claimed it for Spain.

prompt: The name "America" comes from which explorer?
explain: The word America was first used for the lands Amerigo Vespucci visited. In Latin his name is Americus Vespucius.

prompt: Explorer Amerigo Vespucci was born in which city?
explain: Vespucci was born in Florence, Italy, and later worked in Seville, Spain.

prompt: Bartolome de Las Casas spent his life doing what?
choices: Leading the conquest of the Inca
Protesting the mistreatment of Native peoples
explain: Las Casas, a Spanish missionary, devoted his life to protesting the mistreatment of Native peoples.

prompt: In what year did the Mexican Revolution begin?
explain: The Mexican Revolution lasted from 1910 to 1920.

prompt: The Mexican Revolution began with the overthrow of which leader?
explain: The revolution began with the overthrow of Porfirio Diaz, whose policies favored a small rich group.

prompt: Which of these leaders fought in the Mexican Revolution?
explain: Emiliano Zapata, Pancho Villa, and Francisco Madero all gathered supporters in the Mexican Revolution.

prompt: During the Mexican Revolution, a new constitution for Mexico was written in what year?
explain: Venustiano Carranza oversaw the writing of Mexico's constitution of 1917.

prompt: Simon Bolivar was born in which city?
explain: Bolivar was born in Caracas in 1783.

prompt: Simon Bolivar led revolutions against Spanish rule in which of these present-day countries?
explain: Bolivar led the fight in New Granada (now Colombia, Venezuela, and Ecuador), Peru, and Bolivia.

prompt: Who helped Simon Bolivar win independence for Ecuador in 1822?
explain: With the help of Antonio Sucre, Bolivar secured Ecuador's independence in 1822.

prompt: Jose de San Martin is a national hero of which country?
explain: San Martin is a national hero of Argentina. He also helped free Chile and Peru from Spain.

prompt: Jose de San Martin's boldest plan was to lead his army across which mountains?
explain: San Martin led an army over the Andes, a very hard march.

prompt: After Jose de San Martin freed Chile in 1817, he turned the country over to whom?
explain: San Martin liberated Chile in 1817 and turned it over to Bernardo O'Higgins.

prompt: Which leader finished freeing Peru after Jose de San Martin stepped aside in 1822?
explain: After meeting Bolivar in 1822, San Martin went into exile and left Bolivar to finish freeing Peru.

prompt: Benito Juarez, a national hero and president of Mexico, belonged to which Native people?
explain: Juarez was a Zapotec Indian from Oaxaca, Mexico.

prompt: In the 1860s, which country invaded Mexico and put Maximilian of Austria in power?
explain: The French under Napoleon III occupied Mexico and made Maximilian ruler in 1864. Juarez later defeated him.

prompt: In 1791, what did Toussaint Louverture join in Saint-Domingue?
explain: In 1791 Toussaint joined a slave rebellion and soon built an army of his own.

prompt: Why did Toussaint Louverture switch to fight for France in 1794?
choices: France had ended slavery, and Spain had not
Spain had already lost the war
explain: He switched sides because France, unlike Spain, had recently abolished slavery.

prompt: What happened to Toussaint Louverture in 1802?
choices: He was crowned emperor of Haiti
He moved to the United States
The French removed him from power, and he died in custody in France
explain: A French force deposed Toussaint in 1802, and he died in custody in France.

prompt: Who proclaimed Haiti's independence on January 1, 1804?
explain: Dessalines proclaimed Haiti independent on January 1, 1804. Toussaint had died in France in 1803.

prompt: The name Haiti comes from the language of which Native people?
explain: Dessalines gave the new country the Arawak-based name Haiti.

prompt: In 1802, what did Napoleon say he planned to do in Saint-Domingue that made Dessalines rebel?
explain: When it became clear in 1802 that Napoleon meant to bring back slavery, Dessalines and other leaders rebelled and drove out the French.

prompt: Before selling Louisiana, Napoleon wanted to take back which sugar colony from a slave rebellion?
explain: Napoleon planned to recapture the sugar colony of Saint-Domingue (Haiti) from a slave rebellion.

prompt: In 1803, the United States bought the Louisiana Territory from which country?
explain: The United States bought Louisiana from France in 1803 for $15 million.

prompt: Which country first tried to build a canal across Panama, starting in 1880?
explain: The French, led by Ferdinand de Lesseps, began digging in 1880.

prompt: Ferdinand de Lesseps, who led the French canal project in Panama, had earlier built which canal?
choices: The Erie Canal in New York
explain: De Lesseps was the builder of the Suez Canal in Egypt.

prompt: What worked against the French effort to build the Panama Canal?
choices: Tropical diseases like malaria and yellow fever
explain: Malaria, yellow fever, and other tropical diseases worked against the French project.

prompt: In 1903, Panama declared independence from which country?
explain: Panama declared independence from Colombia on November 3, 1903.

prompt: On what date was the Panama Canal turned over to Panama?
explain: The 1977 treaties said the canal would go to Panama on December 31, 1999.

prompt: What did the Monroe Doctrine of 1823 tell European countries?
choices: Spain owned all of South America
The Americas were closed to new European colonies
The United States would buy Canada
explain: President Monroe said the American continents were no longer open to colonization by European powers.

prompt: In 1836, Texas won a war of independence against which country?
explain: Texas won its war of independence against Mexico in 1836.

prompt: The Spanish-American War of 1898 ended which country's colonial empire in the Western Hemisphere?
explain: The war ended Spain's colonial empire in the Western Hemisphere.

prompt: After the Spanish-American War, Spain gave which Caribbean island to the United States?
explain: The Treaty of Paris made Spain give Puerto Rico and Guam to the United States.

prompt: Before the United States joined the war in 1898, Cuban rebels had been fighting for what?
explain: Cuban rebels fought for about three years for independence from Spanish rule.

prompt: Which U.S. president issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863?
explain: Lincoln's proclamation declared enslaved people in the rebelling states free.

prompt: In 1911, which American explorer was led to Machu Picchu by a local resident and began studying it?
explain: A Quechua-speaking resident led Hiram Bingham to Machu Picchu in 1911, and Bingham began scientific study of the site.

prompt: In dates like 1200 BCE, what does BCE mean?
explain: BCE marks dates before the Common Era. CE marks dates in our own era.

prompt: Which of these years came earliest?
explain: BCE years count down toward year 1, so 1200 BCE is earlier than 400 BCE. All BCE years come before CE years.

prompt: Which of these events happened most recently?
choices: Cahokia was at its height (about 1100 CE)
The Aztec began building Tenochtitlan (1325 CE)
explain: 1325 CE is the latest of these dates. The Olmec dates are BCE, so they are the oldest.

prompt: Which of these is a primary source about an event?
choices: A diary written by someone during the event
explain: Diaries and letters from the time are primary sources.

prompt: A map made in the 1960s showing World War II battle sites is what kind of source?
explain: A secondary source is made after the fact. The map was made about 20 years after the war.

prompt: Why do historians check a source against other sources?
choices: To find out how much it cost
To see whether other evidence supports it
explain: Historians look for corroboration, meaning other evidence that agrees with a source.

prompt: A general wrote a letter about a battle he led. Why should a historian read it with care?
choices: Generals did not know how to write
People often describe themselves in the best light
explain: Writers often present themselves in the best light, so historians ask whether the author had an agenda.
